Validate the following vignette.

Patient demographics:
  age: 50
  gender: Male
  ethnicity: African
  relationship_status: Married
  occupation: Plumber
  trauma_type: Assault
  pcl5: 73

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Threat: Safe Zone Only: I only feel safe in a very limited number of places, Startle to Movement: Unexpected movement nearby causes me to react as if I am in danger, Sleep Problems: Trouble falling or staying asleep
  Memory: Guilt on Recall: When I remember the event I feel intense guilt, Visual Memories: My memories of the frightening event are mostly pictures or images., Nonverbal Memory: I can't seem to put the frightening event into words.
  Negative Appraisals: No Longer Capable: I am no longer capable of doing the things that defined me, Injustice: What happened to me was deeply unfair and nothing has been done about it, Self-Doubt: I can't trust that I will do the right thing

Vignette:
Samuel, a 50-year-old African American man, had always prided himself on his reliability and skill as a plumber, a trade he’d practiced for over thirty years. His life with his wife, rooted in their community, felt stable and predictable until an evening six months ago shattered that sense of security. He had been called to an emergency, a burst pipe in the dimly lit, labyrinthine basement of an old apartment building on the city's outskirts. As he navigated the unfamiliar corridors, his tools clanking softly, a figure suddenly emerged from behind a large boiler, striking him from behind and demanding his wallet. The assault was swift and brutal, leaving him disoriented and bruised, his tools scattered across the grimy floor as the assailant vanished into the shadows as quickly as they appeared.

In the aftermath, Samuel found himself struggling to piece together what had happened. His memories of the frightening event were mostly pictures or images – the glint of metal, the sudden lunge, the dark figure disappearing. What was most distressing was that he couldn't seem to put the frightening event into words; the narrative felt fragmented and elusive, yet the visual flashes were vivid and intrusive. When these memories surfaced, an intense, gnawing guilt would wash over him. He replayed the scene endlessly, questioning if he could have done something differently, if he should have been more aware, stronger, faster. This self-reproach fed a pervasive sense of self-doubt; he couldn't trust that he would do the right thing if faced with danger again, or even in everyday decisions.

The incident profoundly altered Samuel's world. He now only felt safe in a very limited number of places, primarily his home and his small, familiar workshop. The thought of venturing into unfamiliar basements or poorly lit commercial buildings, once routine aspects of his job, now filled him with dread. He started turning down jobs that required working alone in such environments, or those that took him to parts of the city he didn't know intimately. This shift began to impact his livelihood, as his reputation for taking on any job, no matter how challenging, slowly eroded. His body, too, had changed. Unexpected movement nearby, a sudden shadow, or a door closing abruptly would cause him to react as if he were in danger, his heart pounding, muscles tensing. At home, his wife noticed his heightened vigilance and the way he would flinch at sudden noises. Sleep offered no respite; he had trouble falling or staying asleep, his nights often punctuated by restless tossing and turning, or waking suddenly from vivid, disquieting images.

Samuel had come to believe that he was no longer capable of doing the things that defined him. The man who could fix anything, who was fearless in the face of complex plumbing emergencies, felt diminished. He saw his hesitation to take jobs as a failure, a sign that the assault had irrevocably broken something within him. What happened to him felt deeply unfair, a cruel twist of fate for which nothing had been done; the police investigation had yielded no arrests, leaving him with a profound sense of injustice. The world felt like a more dangerous, unpredictable place, and he, Samuel, was no longer the man equipped to navigate it. The cumulative weight of these changes, the strain on his business, and the growing distance he felt from his old self, finally brought him to seek help. He wasn't sure what he hoped for, perhaps just to understand why he couldn't shake the feeling that he was perpetually on the brink of another catastrophe, or why the guilt refused to leave him.
